title: China doesn’t need to dominate the world to threaten Australia’s security | The Strategist
paragraphs: This week, former Australian Defence Force chief Chris Barrie said he did not see any evidence from China ‘of global aspirations and global dominance aspirations that we’ve seen out of the United States’ . He also called for Australia to scrap the AUKUS submarine program.

Barrie, who was chief of defence force from 1998 to 2002, made the remarks while presenting a report of the so-called inquiry into AUKUS, which he co-authored with former environment minister Peter Garrett. Although presented as an independent assessment, the exercise attracted criticism over its impartiality, with Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy rightly describing it as ‘a stitch-up from day one’.

Barrie’s whataboutism on the United States rests on false equivalence. The US does maintain a worldwide network of military bases, alliances and security commitments. In doing so, it has provided a security foundation for partners without requiring them to change their political values or systems. Yes, its record includes interventions that have been costly, misguided and damaging to its international standing. All of these have been transparent and subject to democratic oversight and review. Australia has participated in some of those campaigns, and from Vietnam to Iraq we have been willing to examine what they achieved and what they cost us.
